findings.summary: The headline facts assert processor.PeakConcurrency(subjectKey) == 1 while running a one-worker pool, so that particular assertion is weak; the dedicated key fact carries the real per-key single-flight evidence.
findings.detail: SaveChainHarness facts create the worker with workerCount: 1, so per-key concurrency can never exceed 1 irrespective of queue mechanics; the PeakConcurrency assertion is therefore near-tautological. The requirement-8 fact (WorkItemKeyRemainsVersionBlindAndSingleFlightIsPerItemConnectionAndSurface) independently exercises the real LibraryWorkQueue: a version-only difference is Coalesced while pending and InFlight while processing, a distinct surface is Accepted while the primary key is in flight, and the key-equality assertions cover item/connection/surface. This is sufficient evidence for the acceptance criterion; the workerCount-1 assertion is redundant rather than false.
findings.recommended_action: No change required; optional future strengthening could run two workers to make the headline PeakConcurrency assertion non-trivial.

findings.summary: Four helper facts drive ConfigurationSnapshotService.TryReplace directly rather than the full Plugin.UpdateConfiguration save path.
findings.detail: TheStaleBasisReenqueueIsIssuedOnlyAfterTheInFlightSlotIsReleased, StoppedQueueDropsTheStaleBasisReenqueue, and FullQueueDropsTheStaleBasisReenqueue activate the new version via Phase6.Configuration.TryReplace. The facts under test (worker re-enqueue ordering, stopped/full queue drop, and versions-blind key mechanics) do not depend on the plugin save path, and the headline save-while-pending, save-while-in-flight, second-advance, and changed-item facts do exercise the real Plugin.UpdateConfiguration -> TryActivateConfiguration -> trigger.RequestReconciliation path. The acceptance criterion (drives the real save path/post-save trigger/queue/worker/processor chain) is met by the matrix as a whole.

findings.summary: The only logic double is the classification-gate ScriptedProcessor, and it is necessary and disclosed.
findings.detail: The real MetadataReconciliationProcessor checks item.ConfigurationVersion before resolve/eligibility (clause 5), so a real non-version discard always carries the current version and is also blocked by the worker's same-version guard; the gate can only be isolated by supplying the classification directly. NonVersionDiscardsDoNotReenqueue wraps ScriptedProcessor in the real ChainRecordingProcessor and drives the real LibraryWorkWorker and real LibraryWorkQueue, so the gate under test is the production worker. The real-chain no-re-enqueue for all four classifications is separately covered by the changed-item theory. Disclosed in worker-report.json (interpretations/known_limitations).
